Tech for public good but employees are treated so badly

Pros

If you're mid-career you can finish your work in a day or two and lepak the rest. Flexible work hours. nobody cares whether youre in the office or not. One of few workplaces like this these days. They endeavour to do good things for Singapore citizens and that is cool. Really interesting products and problems to solve.

Cons

Extremely low maturity. Most employees are fresh grads or in their first or second job. Way too many came straight from NUS/NTU to OGP and have no idea what other workplaces are like. They bring their weird mean girls politicking to the office - truly shocking that adults behave this way. use words like "retardmaxxing" in their presentations - high ignorance. Low self-awareness and extremely delicate thin skin so if you try to name the gaps to fix them, you will be labelled the problem. Low risk tolerance. Not confident to take bold risks that good product teams require. Low accountability, play the blame game for weeks rather than actually get work done. Slow to iterate and risk-averse - how to pretend you work in tech like that? Tall poppy syndrome and they have a special vendetta against ex-big tech employees. Hierarchical and slow. Despite having little experience they think they are better than the rest of civil service and go so far as to include this fact in written documents. Gap between what they preach and how they behave. Don't walk the talk of the workplace values and enable playground-like behaviour in their teams. No health insurance. Little to no benefits. Expect to spend a lot out of pocket if you have existing private doctors youre seeing. If you can tahan polyclinics & restructured hospitals - great news that's free. Could list many more but these are the key takeaways. I read the (bad) reviews before accepting but thought it would be okay for a while - I was wrong. it is truly terrible and I wouldn't wish this on an enemy. Hands down the most toxic workplace I've ever experienced in my long career.

Pros

Depending on which product team you get assigned to, your teammates can either be very collaborative or full of wannabe lone wolf rockstars who refuse to communicate. Encourages learning (budget given) but no space for trial and error, despite claims of learning from mistakes. Goes right onto your perf evals as "no impact".

Cons

Too many middle managers whose idea of retaining their jobs is by making the workplace a hostile environment. All talk, no visible product impact themselves. Has made OGP a toxic workplace. All the good folks have left. Products created can be a duplicate of other products that already exists elsewhere in govt, not sure why resources are wasted just to make a mess in the govt apps ecosystem.

A lot of bus drivers -- SBS should recruit from here.

Pros

- Good work-life balance & a lot of autonomy to work on things you want. - Decent Salary

Cons

- Only visibility matters; from public perception standpoint. Actual outcomes don't, even if your product produces actual public good & can get taken away from you and given to another person. - Culture of dysfunction and managing people out if you "dont perform" (which is entirely subjective) - Terrible managers who have no backbone and are just "yes" man to CEO. They dont do much all day except "manage" and will throw you under the bus if it will help their case. - Quite a boys club and culture can be quite misogynistic at times. Aggressive behaviour is not just condone but rewarded.
